answer: Sybil attacks die on cost, not cleverness. Each identity posts a bond locked for a term and slashed if review finds the account fabricated. One fake account costs only its bond, but standing cannot grow without many bonds at once, and locked stake is public, so a thousand look-alike identities show as a thousand entries with collateral idle, not one voice. The velvet part: honest users pay nothing, since the bond returns untouched. The garden stays open to newcomers on a modest deposit while a fake farm must front the full sum each time, so attacker price grows. Equilibrium, not a spiral.
